prerequisites: Basic training in electronic circuit design: design tools like Proteus, Cadence, etc.
Knowledge of programming languages: C language, Java

learning_outcomes.text: Know how to select the most suitable option for the control circuit, depending on the application, number of units, working environment.
Know the design phases of digital ASICs, as well as the basic concepts about Test.
Know the manufacturing processes of ASICs.
Know how to design digital circuits of medium complexity, using schematic entry.
Know how to design digital circuits of medium complexity, using hardware description languages.
Know the basic power circuits, which act as an intermediate between digital stages and power loads.
Select the necessary heat sinks for power devices.
Ability to evaluate and select commercial communication modules, according to the application.

Prepare technical specifications that allow problems in mechatronics engineering to be formulated, maintaining a global and integrative vision and using prescriptive, procedural or performance specifications as appropriate.
Organize conceptual design activity to support decision-making and selection among possible solutions to an engineering problem.

Students know how to apply the acquired knowledge and their ability to solve problems in new or little-known environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their area of study.
Students know how to communicate their conclusions and the knowledge and ultimate reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences in a clear and unambiguous way.
Students possess the learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a way that will largely be self-directed or autonomous.
Select the most suitable programmable logic devices in each case for the design of mechatronic systems, manage their development systems and design the interface stages that may be necessary.
Incorporate the necessary electrical, hydraulic and pneumatic sensors and actuators depending on the characteristics of the mechatronic system, its specifications and its integration.
Select electronic devices for instrumentation and control that allow conditioning and processing analog and digital signals from sensors and sent to typical actuators of a mechatronic system.

syllabus_topics: Design of digital circuits with Programmable Logic Devices: FPGA, PLDs.
Introduction to Design and Testability of Application-Specific Integrated Circuits
1.-Design of application-specific integrated circuits ASICs (fullcustom, semicustom)
5.2 Specific circuits: power drivers, bluetooth modules
Practice 1. Design of an adder/subtractor circuit (Quartus II)
Practice 4: Connection of bluetooth module to SPI in PLD

assessment_methods.method: Written tests/deliverables: objective tests, short-answer tests and/or development tests (PE)
Oral tests (individual, group, presentation of individual topics-works, etc.) (PO)

assessment_rules: For ordinary evaluation, a minimum score of four points is required in each evaluable section. If the minimum is not reached in the reports, students can complete the grade with a written test. The final grade is calculated as: 0.2*PE + 0.5*PO + 0.2*IP + 0.1*AP. For extraordinary evaluation, the 10% of the attitude scales is transferred to the practice reports section, resulting in a final grade of: 0.2*PE + 0.5*PO + 0.3*IP.
